gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus cuts its 240V output while it is recharging from 120V AC, so a 240V well pump stops whenever the station is topped up from a 120V generator or wall outlet unless Anker's $399.99 240V Bypass Charging Cable is added. None states either that the Growatt HELIOS 3600 only gives 240V when two units are paired through a $139 Double Voltage Power Hub.
standout_why: I opened offgridbenchmark.com (2026-11-02), holdbackup.com (2026-10-26) and thewell.guide (2026-10-22), plus Anker's own well-pump guide, which offgridbenchmark cites. All four cover 240V versus 120V, transfer switches and backfeed, and starting surge. offgridbenchmark and thewell.guide also cover 2-wire versus 3-wire pumps, and offgridbenchmark covers Franklin's start and stop order and its warning about soft starters. offgridbenchmark lists the Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus as a 240V station but does not say the 240V output stops while the unit charges on 120V AC. None of the four mentions recharging while the pump runs, pass-through or bypass charging, or that some '240V capable' stations need a second unit and a hub. Anker's well-pump guide says a 240V pump starts only if the battery system's LRA covers the pump's LRA, but it never mentions the F3800 Plus charging limit. This decides what goes in the cart: an F3800 Plus kit that will be recharged from a generator needs the bypass cable, and a Growatt kit needs two HELIOS 3600 units plus the hub, not one.
kit_items: 240V power station that gives split-phase 240V from one unit: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus. Its store listing says 120V/240V and 6,000W AC per unit, with NEMA TT-30P and L14-30 ports. One unit covers the pump, so you don't need a second station.

240V recharge path that keeps the pump running: Anker SOLIX 240V Bypass Charging Cable for F3800 Plus. Anker sells it for 'Simultaneous 240V Fast Charging and Power Output' from a 240V wall outlet or gas generator. Without it, charging on 120V AC disables the 240V output the pump needs.
House connection: the Anker Smart Home Power Kit bundle (F3800 Plus + Smart Home Power Kit). Hardwired pumps need transfer equipment installed by an electrician, which all three rival pages also say.

Alternative set (Growatt store): 2× Growatt HELIOS 3600 + Growatt Double Voltage Power Hub. Growatt only offers 240V when two units are paired, and the hub provides one NEMA 6-20 and two NEMA L14-30 outlets. A single HELIOS 3600 is the wrong buy for a 240V pump.

findings.note: The LRA table covers only the E10 system: up to 120 A with one E10 and one battery module, up to 155 A with two or more modules, and up to 275 A with two E10 units. The guide says nothing about the F3800 Plus 120V-charging limit or about bypass charging.
